title: Rate shepherding: graceful limiter recovery, outage fairness, and multi-region SLO alignment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our production limiter fabric has shown two failure modes in recent chaos runs: 1) short-lived control-plane outages cause unfair drop of higher-priority tenants when regional leases rehydrate; 2) bursty traffic combined with cross-region failover triggers global SLO oscillation as tokens are aggressively shed and then reintroduced. Goal: design and ship a resilient limiter behavior we call 'rate shepherding' that preserves tenant fairness across bursts and during limiter outages, minimizes SLO drift across regions, and provides clear operational runbooks. Scope: changes are limited to the admission controller and quota reconciliation paths (no billing changes). This ticket covers design, simulation, implementation of controller heuristics, telemetry, canary rollout, and runbook updates. Success metrics: - Reduce priority inversion incidents in chaos tests from current baseline to <1 per 50 runs. - Maintain P99 latency SLO for host-tier customers within 1.2x during regional failovers. - Restore steady-state token distribution within 30s of limiter recovery for typical burst profiles. Constraints and trade-offs: aggressive pre-allocation reduces latency but increases overcommit risk during simultaneous region failures; conservative draining preserves fairness but can raise short-term tail latency. We'll adopt a hybrid approach: speculative soft-credits + bounded rebalancing windows. High-level solution: 1) Soft-credit reservoir: when a region detects local limiter instability, it temporarily issues short-lived soft-credits to in-flight requests to avoid hard rejects for latency-sensitive routes. Soft-credits are time-limited and accounted-for in later reconciliation. 2) Ranked replenishment: on limiter rehydration, replenish tenant tokens with a weighted-fair algorithm that prefers historically under-served clients for the last 60s and respects tenant priority and SLA tiers. 3) Conservative cross-region failover: add a multi-phase failover where traffic is shifted in bounded increments (5%-30% windows) with feedback from remote SLO probes before full migration. 4) Circuit breaker integration: when underlying admission backends report persistent errors, circuit trips to soft-credit-only mode with explicit telemetry and alerting. 5) Observability/telemetry: new metrics and dashboards for soft-credit issuance, speculative rebalances, and time-to-reconcile. Implementation plan: - Simulation & canary harness updates (locally and on staging). - Runtime admission controller changes with feature flag (rate_shepherding_v1). - Telemetry and SLO probe additions. - Canary rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on regression. - Runbook & playbook updates for on-call. Risks: incorrect accounting could allow tenants to exceed committed throughput; ensure reconciliation is idempotent. Rollback plan: feature flag off, and a compensating reconciliation job that drains soft-credits.
